Why do I continually get angry at games even though I consciously know there's no reason to be angry? Anything I can do to get rid of this habit?

You get angry at games because they frustrate you before they reward you. It's also the reason why you like games, beating what makes you angry makes you happy, but then there is already the next challenge. To get rid of it you could try to study game mechanics and game design, but it might also take some of the fun out of gaming.

Like, if I die in Counter-Strike, I know exactly what I did wrong, and why I died, also why my aim was off point. But I still get so angry for some reason. I sometimes get mad even when I win, because I died unnecessarily a few rounds back...

The anger makes you try again and do better and the feeling you get when you master the move you failed so many times before makes you enduring the same again.

Not everyone gets the same anger and reward feelings though. For some people those kind of games are relaxing, for some they are stressing.

Maybe your reaction is a learned reaction? Did you observe this same type of anger response from some adult or sibling that helped raise you? Maybe anger involving sporting events, or something equally unworthy of anger?

I've noticed I get angry at some of the same things my father did. He was rather vocal about his frustration. Then one day I realized I didn't care about those things as much as dad, and stopped being as angry about matters I felt were trivial.

Knowing is half the battle...
Not a learned reaction. My parents are as good as they come.

It could be that you are mad about something else, and use games as an excuse to let yourself express it.

Or maybe it's your diet. If you don't eat enough veggies and too much meat, you could be more likely to anger quicker. Not a fact, but something I found that happened to myself.

Or it's too much sugar, caffeine, or energy drinks?

Or you are simply playing a frustrating game. I played some league earlier and I yelled out loud four times.

It's hard to say what the solution for your problem should be, since I am not sure what the cause of it is.

Like, if I die in Counter-Strike, I know exactly what I did wrong, and why I died, also why my aim was off point. But I still get so angry for some reason. I sometimes get mad even when I win, because I died unnecessarily a few rounds back...
You could simply be passionate about the game. Too many variables.
Is it contained to this particular game or does the spill to other things? If just this game, then you are fine, we all have something small like that.

Technically, nothing is a false reality. Everything you do is real. Our imagination, and our thoughts, while not tangible, are real. So when you play a video game you are actually doing something, and not being able to achieve your goals within that real makes you frustrated. Although for me, when a video game annoys me, I just take a break, and go back to it the next day. I don't flip out over it. I've never thrown a video game controller.
